newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik leader dismisses four defence officials.
newsitem.headline: Tajik leader dismisses four defence officials.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov sacked four deputy defence ministers on Wednesday and promised a shake-up of the former Soviet republic's security structures.
"The decision was taken because of the serious shortcomings in their work," Rakhmonov's spokesman Zafar Saidov told reporters in the capital Dushanbe.

Defence Minister Sherali Khayrullayev was also given a "final warning" to improve his own performance, Saidov said, citing poor discipline within the army and misuse of army property as reasons for the sackings.
Official sources, however, say the Tajik government's military reverses against Islamist opposition guerrillas last year was the principal reason for the firings.
"It is the first step to reforming the armed forces of Tajikistan," said Saidov, who said the government was now scrutinising the performance of the interior and security ministries.
The embattled president is currently negotiating with the Islamist opposition to end a bloody four-year civil war which has left tens of thousands dead and many more homeless.
But Rakhmonov's grip on the mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China is shaky -- diplomats estimate he controls only 15-20 percent of the republic -- as is his hold on the army.

Last month, the commander of an elite government unit moved his tanks against one of Tajikistan's myriad armed bands without consulting Rakhmonov and ignored for some time the president's repeated exhortations to return to barracks.
